notes.text: Fresh from the arson of the Sleeping Giant, the party alongisde Daran Edermath, made their way straight to Tresendar Manor (via a quick stop to receive a blessing from Sister Garaele), opting to keep momentum and strike while the Redbrands were still unprepared.

They descended into the cellar, exploring the first set of storage rooms, finding an empty sleeping area, and a secret door. While investigating the tunnel to the cavern beyond the door, they drew the notice of the Nothic that had taken up residence and struck a deal with the Redbrands - protection for fresh meat. Milo engaged in a telepathic conversation with the Nothic, it showed him his own most traumatic event, and indicated it had other secrets it might be willing to trade for. Eventually Milo opted to retreat from the creature, at which point it raised the alarm about the intruders. The three bugbears resident in the barracks came running, and a heated battle ensued, with the Nothic sniping with its Rotting Gaze, Thoren coming close to death, and Xander almost abducted by a bugbear.

Making their way deeper into the complex, they found an alchemical laboratory which was being used to produce potions of invisibility, and were seen by the rat familiar of the wizard Glasstaff, who ran up his secret escape stairs right into the waiting party. With some lucky quick thinking and movement (and the previous failure of the party to remove his go-bag from the cistern), Glasstaff managed to down a potion of invisibility and escape from the Tresendar crypts. After a little more fighting and clearing of undead, the party found a few more Redbrands and the severely injured bugbear keeping hostages in the prison cells - they struck a deal to let the thugs leave with their lives - both sides kept to the deal and the hostages (Thel Dendrar's wife and two teenage children) were safely freed.

Sildar was surprised and angry to discover his colleague Iarno Albrek had fallen in league with the black spider, and is interested in tracking him down. He also recommended the party try to make contact with a druid named Reidoth who wanders the forests and foothills to the Northwest, as he may know where the Cragmaw Castle lies Halia Thornton was impressed with the work, including the ruthless tactics employed. She  supplied the party with a map of the region, which had some marked ruined forts as well as the locations of Thundertree and Wyvern Tor Daran wanted to ensure the party would hold up their end of the deal to find out the source of the sapblight zombies, though found himself in no shape to accompany them.

Linene Graywind supplied the party with a monetary reward from the merchants of the town for dealing with the Redbrands, and gave them access to a few specialised magical items imported for particularly well-off and demanding prospectors. She had available: ○ Rope of climbing (800GP) ○ 4 potions of gaseous form (400 all together) ○ Glamoured studded leather armor The party then headed out to Thundertree, travelling through a rainy thunderstorm. ON the second night, they witnessed a wandering Auroksis, a gargantuan creature that grazes on entire trees, and has a school of flying remora-like creatures accompanying it. The next day they arrived in Thundertree, a seemingly abandoned town near the pyroclastic flow of an ancient eruption. They made their way inside the inn, and found it full of ash and bodies. As Milo was inspecting one, a swarm of ash zombies awoke, and a battle was about to begin.

loreEntries.title: The Veil
loreEntries.body:
The Veil
    • Reclusive and shadowy criminal network
    • Deal in weapons smuggling, mercenary supplies, assassinations and thieving
    • Often use the information their agents learn on assignments against clients to blackmail or bribe them
    • There’s a story about their leader being an immortal wizard
    • Headquarters in Windtide

loreEntries.title: The Silver Hand
loreEntries.body:
The Silver Hand
    • A Mafia-style grouping of five families runs this shady mercenary company
    • While anyone who had coin could retain their services, they worked closely with the Kolus Union before Contact, helping to maintain colonial outposts, manage work crews and caravans, and guarding borders. In recent years their activity in the New Union seems to have increased and become more criminal, competing with the Veil.
    • Headquarted in Angard’s Rest in Tolaur

loreEntries.title: The Wild's Run
loreEntries.body:
The Wild’s Run
    • Hunters/rangers/monster slayers for hire
    • Nose-to-tail philosophy
    • Hate trophy hunting, all kills must be necessary for balance

loreEntries.title: Helldiver's Club
loreEntries.body:
The Helldivers Club
    • A mercenary/adventuring network who hire out their services. Has a franchise structure - often an established adventuring group will get bought out and assimilated into the overall organisation
    • Expedition escort services, find and retrieve missions, eliminating monsters or fiends

loreEntries.title: The Archivex
loreEntries.body:
The Archivex 
    • Network of libraries and archaeological societies, headquartered in Woldruum. Patron god is Einar, although not all affiliates are religious
    • Monks, knowledge clerics, bards, wizards
    • Aim to preserve balance by sequestering powerful artifacts, or destroying them if need be

loreEntries.title: Contact
loreEntries.body:
Contact was an earthshattering event for every person in Novalis

Contact began when the Human King Arnoud Vatim ordered his Admiral Youn Firthssin to sail the newly constructed and magically-powered 7 ship airfleet over the great waterwaste to the West, with the intent of founding a new colony. At this time there were no other known advanced races to the people of Bostheim, and the Waterwaste had never been crossed on account of the Vasttide - a regular, giant wave originating from the North. After a month long journey, the airfleet arrived on the Eastern shores of Al'oker at the elven settlement of Mithra. The fleet was immediately met by an elven dragonrider, but the crew of Admiral Firthssin's ship had never seen a tame dragon, and opened fire in fear, prompting a swift rallying of the elven dragonflight guard and destruction of the airfleet.

Two years later, the Dragonflight Advance invaded Bostheim's western shores where Forrgald meets the Waterwaste. The Kolus Union had been busy building Air Frigates with the agility and fireproofing to withstand dragon attacks. However, they were powered with divine magic granted (and being constantly channelled) by the Church of Kolus. As the Dragonflight approached land, all connection to Kolus suddenly disappeared. Every cleric and all magic sustained by him became suddenly mundane. The Airfleet fell from the sky.

The Dragonflight easily overpowered the Union’s cavalry-based armies, and razed the westernmost Pentacity of Darkwall. For unknown reasons, the Helath immediately called a truce in exchange for the annexation of the ruins of Darkwall and surrounding land. That region is now magically shrouded and barriered - no-one on Bostheim knows what is happening inside. 

With the sudden loss of power and destruction of much of the Union’s army, the slaves revolted and drove out their former masters.

loreEntries.title: The Gods
loreEntries.body:
The gods of Novalis all used to be mortals, though they no longer bear much resemblance to their mortal forms. Divine power comes from worship in whatever form is demanded by the gods. It is well-known that all of the gods ascended long ago, and none have been added since. The gods can, and have visited Novalis frequently, to intervene in wars, meet with Kings, and to have families.

Before the gods there were Titans. These were otherworldly manifestations of the elements and of chaos. The titans acted as reavers and renewers of worlds, breaking down living things, planets and even stars to their constituent parts, so they could be remade. The gods were once mortals who sensed the return of the Titans, and through now-lost magic managed to ascend to a level of power where they could challenge the Titans. A key component of this ritual was the Heaven’s Chain, a metaphysical construct that forces the Divine Realm of Elysium apart from the Material Plane. Maintaining this construct is essential to maintaining the concept and order of Divinity. Prayer, worship, divine power and the Gods themselves travel along the Chain.
Many other powerful beings exist across the planes, but no others are considered Divine. 

Kolus (War)
    • God of blood and songs
    • A cunning military strategist who understands the worth of both tactics and fury. Teaches that all means justify a victory
    • Leads the divine war effort against Hell and Titans
Griig (Tempest)
    • God of storms and fortitude
    • The source of lightning and wind in the Material Plane
    • Said to have been a cloud giant in life, and is worshipped by the Cloud Giants of Ryvast
Velania (Death)
    • God of balance and regeneration
    • Stands at the entrance to The Pit and guards all other realms from Hell and The Abyss
    • Guides souls to their correct place after death
    • Married to Roke since they were mortals
The Living Shadow (Trickery)
    • God of ancestors and secrets
    • Good-natured keeper of the knowledge of gods
    • When someone dies, The Living Shadow interviews them in a windowless, doorless room floating in the Astral Sea. It ascertains all knowledge available to that being and remembers it
Roke (Life)
    • God of pleasure and vitality
    • Guides new souls to bodies - without him all babies would be born dead
Einar (Knowledge)
    • God of exploration and craft
    • Builds god weapons and spies on titans
    • Brother of Drathir
Drathir (Light)
    • God of fire and chaos
    • Maintains divinity by fuelling the heaven’s chain
    • Einar and Drathir are designer and builder of the weapons and defences of Elysium
The Whispered Wind (Nature)
    • Emotionless, faceless
    • When it was a mortal, it was an Orcish child that lived and died in the wilderness with no contact
    • Spends most of its time on the Material Plane, tending it like a garden
